newsitem.title: USA: Colorful parade of U.S. junk bond issuers expected.
newsitem.headline: Colorful parade of U.S. junk bond issuers expected.

text.p: Cheered on by money managers with spare cash to invest, a variety of diverse issuers are expected to sell around $2 billion in new high-yield corporate bonds in the U.S. this week, syndicate officials said.
"I see a diverse group of deals this week from many different industries," said one syndicate official.
"What's interesting is that despite (Federal Reserve Chairman) Greenspan's comments and a sell-off in the Treasury and equity markets, it's still business as usual in high yield."

High-yield issuers expected to hit the market this week include: AMC Entertainment Inc, one of the largest U.S. movie theater companies; Hollinger International, an international newspaper publishing company; Lomak Petroleum, an oil and gas development company; and Booth Creek Ski Holdings Inc, a privately-held ski resort company.
Low interest rates and strong buyside demand are also expected to bring more high-grade supply this week.
"Issuers are getting jittery about the possibilty of a rate increase. They are feeling the pressure to tap the market while good conditions last," one syndicate official said.
Sources said 360 Communications Co, a cellular and long-distance telephone and paging-service provider, is expected to sell $200 million in 12-year bonds via Salomon Brothers Inc later this week.

TCI Communications Inc is also expected to sell $500 million in capital securities via Merrill Lynch & Co and Lehman Brothers Inc. The offering of 30-year securities, which are non-callable for 10 years, was held over from last week's schedule, an official said.
As of Monday morning, Smith Barney Holdings sold $250 million in seven percent seven-year notes through Smith Barney Inc.
